messages.content: Indianapolis just sent a wrinkle. Friday check-in is now at the badge-controlled rehab tower, still 7 a.m., and they want me to bring one extra rolling demo bag. Is rideshare still sane or do I need a little rental car?

Small rental is worth it only if you need to self-park or shuttle equipment without a host. Otherwise I’d lead with a reserved XL rideshare: lobby by 6:00, pickup 6:10, tower drop around 6:30-6:40. It is cheaper and avoids downtown parking. The risk is an app cancellation, not traffic; the access-controlled tower means the host meeting you at the curb matters more than having your own car.
I do not want to drive downtown unless it materially helps. The extra bag is a rolling soft case, awkward but not huge.

Then I would not rent yet. Use an XL from the airport to the hotel Thursday, ask the suite hotel for a bell cart, and use a reserved XL Friday morning. I’ll note that the host should meet you curbside at the rehab tower staff entrance so you are not trying to badge in while managing both bags.
Add a backup if the app flakes.

Backup stack: reserve the XL, ask the front desk Thursday night for their early-morning taxi or car-service number, and have that number saved. If no driver is assigned by 6:20, call the taxi while keeping the app active. That still preserves a cushion before 7:00.
And please recheck Sunday. I do not want the extra bag stuck behind a locked door.

Sunday still fits. After the Saturday 2:30 wrap, leave the extra bag in the host’s secured storage only if they confirm a Sunday access contact. Plan: hotel checkout around 10:45, tower pickup about 11:05-11:15, XL to IND, arrive around noon for the 2:10 return.
Okay, use that. Keep the rental as the emergency fallback only.

Friday: rolling demo bag, bell cart, 6:10 reserved XL, taxi/front-desk backup, host curb meet at the rehab tower. Sunday: checkout, tower pickup, XL to IND for the 2:10 return. messages.content: Switching gears: my partner registered for a mid-December trail race outside Chattanooga. I can leave Tampa after a Friday morning debrief, and I need to be back Sunday night or very early Monday. Can you compare driving versus flying through Atlanta?
Absolutely. I’ll compare it by how much each option protects Sunday night and Monday, not just price. What is the race start area, and is Friday noon the earliest you can leave Tampa?
Race is Sunday at 8 near Raccoon Mountain. Friday noon is realistic, maybe 12:30. One room is fine, queen is okay. I mostly care about not being wrecked for Monday prep.

Driving is the budget play but not the clean one: Tampa to Chattanooga is roughly 9 to 10 hours with stops, so a noon Friday departure lands you late, and Sunday after a shower would put you home around midnight or later. Flying TPA-ATL and renting a car adds airport logistics and two fares, but you’d likely reach Chattanooga Friday by dinner and get home Sunday night with less wear. For this trip, I’d rank fly-via-Atlanta first, drive second only if cost dominates.
Group the lodging the same way. Practical first, then cheapest.

Most practical: Staybridge Suites Chattanooga Downtown/Convention Center. It is not closest to Raccoon Mountain, about 25-30 minutes, but the suite setup is clearer: queen or king studio options, fridge or kitchenette-style storage, coffee maker, indoor pool, and fitness room. No hot tub listed. Good candidate for a 1 p.m. late-checkout request. Better weekend feel: SpringHill Suites Downtown/Cameron Harbor. Mini-fridge and coffee maker listed, pool and fitness, no hot tub shown; a little less kitchen-like. Closest option: the race-area lodge or cabins. Race morning is easiest, but room age, refrigerator details, and late checkout are all unclear.
The race-area lodge sounds risky. Which downtown one gives us the best chance of a post-race shower?

Staybridge is the better bet because the room setup supports keeping food and gear organized until a late checkout; ask for 1 p.m. or 1:30. SpringHill is close behind if they confirm late checkout. The lodge is the weak one: even if it is close, unclear fridge and checkout policies make Sunday awkward. Plain caveat: none of these are showing a confirmed hot tub.
Can Sunday still work through Atlanta if checkout is 1?

Yes, if you target an evening ATL-TPA flight. Example: race starts 8:00, back to hotel around 11:30-12:00, shower and checkout by 1:00, drive to ATL by 3:30-4:00 with buffer. A 7-ish p.m. return from ATL gets you to Tampa around 9-10. If the race runs long, an 8:30-ish return is safer. Driving all the way home Sunday is the plan most likely to wreck Monday.
Do not book until my partner confirms he is okay with the Atlanta drive after racing. But pencil the practical plan.

Penciled as the practical plan: Friday early-afternoon TPA-ATL, midsize rental from ATL, downtown suite hotel Friday-Sunday, Sunday evening ATL-TPA. I’ll keep the full drive as the cost comparison, not the lead option. No booking until he weighs in.
Use the hotel with the clearer fridge and coffee setup. If no hot tub, just say it plainly in the notes.

Got it. I’ll put Staybridge first because the fridge and coffee setup is clearer, then SpringHill as the nicer-feeling backup if its late checkout is better. Race-area lodge stays last with caveats: older or unclear room details, refrigerator not verified, no clear recovery amenities, and uncertain late checkout. Follow-ups before booking: confirm your partner is okay with the ATL drive after racing, call the first two hotels about 1-1:30 late checkout or any shower option after checkout, and price the Friday/Sunday flights plus rental.
